statement: OWNERSET-1.1 (d21 change-discipline family, mechanizing L39) is implemented as a pure function check_ownerset(base: &str, head: &str, path: &RelPath, rule_id: &RuleId) -> Vec<Finding> in crates/enforcer-lang-common/src/rules/change_discipline.rs, matching every `(owner-set` marker LINE (normalized-trim identity, not whole-file byte-equality) present in base against head; a base marker line absent from head is one Finding naming the file + the lost marker text. New marker lines added in head are never flagged. Chosen over a diff-aware Validator seam because none exists yet in enforcer-validator (the trait is single-source ValidationInput); OwnersetValidator adapts the pure function onto that single-source trait by splitting one fixture file on a literal ===HEAD=== delimiter line, so the rule still rides the standard run_fixture_parity harness and the d01 5-way parity oracle without inventing a new crate-wide seam.
why: The workpack's own fallback instruction (no diff-aware seam -> pure function + unit surface) collided with wanting the rule to also participate in the existing fixture/parity harness and registry-record 5-way linkage that every other enforcer-rules record proves through. A single-file-with-delimiter fixture format satisfies both: the pure function is the real, reusable API a future c04 pre-push hook / CI job can call directly with real git blob content, while the Validator adapter is only a harness-compatibility shim for THIS crate's existing test conventions.
howToApply: A future c04 pre-push hook or CI job with real base/head git blobs should call change_discipline::check_ownerset directly, not go through OwnersetValidator/HEAD_DELIMITER — that delimiter and the single-source adapter exist only so this rule's fixtures can be authored as ordinary crate test fixtures and pass through run_fixture_parity like every sibling rule. Any other future diff-aware rule in this crate should follow the same shape: pure fn(base, head, ...) -> Vec<Finding> as the real API, thin single-source Validator adapter only if it needs to ride the existing harness.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-lang-common/src/rules/change_discipline.rs — 13 unit tests green (fixture parity x3, pure-function semantics x6, anti-vacuous guard x1, live-corpus pin x1, registration x1, adapter pass-fixtures x2)

statement: crates/enforcer-lang-common's #[workspace.lints] bans clippy::expect_used and clippy::unwrap_used even inside #[cfg(test)] modules (clippy -D warnings caught `p.parse().expect(...)` and `"OWNERSET-1.1".parse().expect(...)` in test helper functions). Sibling rule modules (fsm.rs, deferred_work.rs) avoid this by never writing a bare test helper that panics — every RuleId/RelPath construction happens either at struct-construction time via a Result-returning `new() -> Result<Self, DecodeError>` with `?`, or inline in a #[test] fn whose own signature returns Result<(), DecodeError> (or Box<dyn Error>) so `?` propagates instead of unwrap/expect.
why: A first draft of change_discipline.rs's test module had two small helper functions `fn path(p: &str) -> RelPath` and `fn rule_id() -> RuleId` that used `.expect("valid literal in test")` for ergonomic call sites — clippy flagged both as `-D clippy::expect-used` violations, failing `cargo clippy -p enforcer-lang-common --all-targets -- -D warnings` even though the crate built and all unit tests passed.
howToApply: When adding test helpers that parse a branded newtype (RuleId, RelPath, etc.) from a string literal in this codebase, make the helper return Result<T, DecodeError> and have every #[test] fn that calls it also return a Result so `?` can propagate — never reach for .expect()/.unwrap() as a shortcut, even in test-only code, because the workspace lint denies both unconditionally (`#[allow]` is also disallowed by pack discipline, so the only fix is refactoring signatures, not suppressing the lint).

evidence.ref: cargo clippy -p enforcer-lang-common --all-targets -- -D warnings — 2 expect_used errors before refactor, 0 after converting path()/rule_id() test helpers and their callers to Result-returning + `?`

statement: Grepping docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/refs/orchestration-lessons.md's ships-via column for every row naming a mechanism (not just prose/vigilance) found a majority still pure-prose: no landed validator/rule-record/CI-hook artifact exists for most rows yet, only L39 (this pack) and a small number of already-built d01-family mechanisms have code behind them. The full per-row breakdown was written to docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/refs/lessons-mechanization-backlog.md for the x05 wave to close systematically rather than being fixed ad hoc by whichever lane happens to notice a row.
why: The sweep duty in this pack asked only to LIST gaps, not build them (out of scope for d21-ownerset's owns:), so surfacing the backlog as a durable doc artifact (rather than just this ndjson note) gives x05 a checkable inventory instead of requiring a re-grep from scratch.
howToApply: x05 (or any future lesson-mechanization lane) should treat lessons-mechanization-backlog.md as the authoritative punch list and update the 'landed?' column in place as each row's mechanism actually ships, rather than re-deriving the list from the ledger each time.
